19988-little-maid-marian.title: Marian
19988-little-maid-marian.creator: Amy E. Blanchard
19988-little-maid-marian.description: A book by Amy E. Blanchard. They talked that way very often, she remembered, and she herself had grown to consider it quite as difficult as did her grandmother, to exercise complete faith. She had made numberless mighty efforts, and yet things did not come out as she supposed they ought.

42351-the-cruise-of-a-schooner.title: The Cruise Of A Schooner
42351-the-cruise-of-a-schooner.creator: Unknown
42351-the-cruise-of-a-schooner.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. In planning an extended trip in this country, or Europe, the first thing one usually does is to consult, if convenient, friends who have been there before. After deciding when you will start, you look up time-tables or the departure of boats, reserve accommodations for your party, pack your grips or trunks, and you are ready to start.

65285-music-and-life-a-study-of-the-rela.title: A Study Of The Relations Between Ourselves And Music
65285-music-and-life-a-study-of-the-rela.creator: Unknown
65285-music-and-life-a-study-of-the-rela.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Any discussion of the art of music,--of its significance in relation to ourselves, of its æsthetic qualities, or of methods of teaching it,--to be comprehensive, must be based on a clear recognition of the one important quality which is inherent in it, which distinguishes it from the other arts and which gives it its peculiar power.

arxiv-2111-07719.title: Eigenvalue ratios for vibrating String equations with concave densities
arxiv-2111-07719.creator: Jihed Hedhly
arxiv-2111-07719.description: Abstract In this paper, we prove the optimal lower bound λ n λ m ≥ ( n m ) 2 \frac{\lambda_{n}}{\lambda_{m}}\geq(\frac{n}{m})^{2} of vibrating string − y ′′ = λ ​ ρ ​ ( x ) ​ y , -y^{\prime\prime}=\lambda\rho(x)y, with Dirichlet boundary conditions for concave densities. Our aproach is based on the method of Huang [Proc. AMS., 1999].

arxiv-2211-12167.title: Global linear stability analysis of kinetic Trapped Ion Mode (TIM) in tokamak plasma using spectral method
arxiv-2211-12167.creator: D. Mandal, M. Lesur, E. Gravier, J. N. Sama, A. Guillevic, Y. Sarazin, X. Garbet
arxiv-2211-12167.description: Abstract Trapped ion modes (TIM) belong to the family of ion temperature gradient (ITG) modes, which are one of the important ingredients in heat turbulent transport at the ion scale in tokamak plasmas. A global linear analysis of a reduced gyro-bounce kinetic model for trapped particle modes is performed, and a spectral method is proposed to solve the dispersion relation.

arxiv-2212-10193.title: Thermodynamics of a continuously monitored double quantum dot heat engine in the repeated interactions framework
arxiv-2212-10193.creator: Laetitia P. Bettmann, Michael J. Kewming, John Goold
arxiv-2212-10193.description: Abstract Understanding the thermodynamic role of measurement in quantum mechanical systems is a burgeoning field of study. In this article, we study a double quantum dot (DQD) connected to two macroscopic fermionic thermal reservoirs. We assume that the DQD is continuously monitored by a quantum point contact (QPC), which serves as a charge detector.

arxiv-2306-07212.title: Polyhedral Complex Extraction from ReLU Networks using Edge Subdivision
arxiv-2306-07212.creator: Arturs Berzins
arxiv-2306-07212.description: Abstract A neural network consisting of piecewise affine building blocks, such as fully-connected layers and ReLU activations, is itself a piecewise affine function supported on a polyhedral complex. This complex has been previously studied to characterize theoretical properties of neural networks, but, in practice, extracting it remains a challenge due to its high combinatorial complexity.

arxiv-2401-07058.title: Does More Advice Help? The Effects of Second Opinions in AI-Assisted Decision Making DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Journal: PACMHCI Volume: x CSCW xxx 11 DOI: xx.xxxx/xxxxxxx CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in HCI CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning
arxiv-2401-07058.creator: Zhuoran Lu, Dakuo Wang, Ming Yin
arxiv-2401-07058.description: Abstract . AI assistance in decision-making has become popular, yet people’s inappropriate reliance on AI often leads to unsatisfactory human-AI collaboration performance. In this paper, through three pre-registered, randomized human subject experiments, we explore whether and how the provision of second opinions may affect decision-makers’ behavior and performance in AI-assisted decision-making.

arxiv-2407-06187.title: JeDi: Joint-Image Diffusion Models for Finetuning-Free Personalized Text-to-Image Generation
arxiv-2407-06187.creator: Yu Zeng, Vishal M. Patel, Haochen Wang, Xun Huang, Ting-Chun Wang, Ming-Yu Liu, Yogesh Balaji
arxiv-2407-06187.description: Abstract Personalized text-to-image generation models enable users to create images that depict their individual possessions in diverse scenes, finding applications in various domains. To achieve the personalization capability, existing methods rely on finetuning a text-to-image foundation model on a user’s custom dataset, which can be non-trivial for general users, resource-intensive, and time-consuming.

arxiv-2512-23512.title: UniHetero: Could Generation Enhance Understanding for Vision-Language-Model at Large Data Scale?

pmc-10611209.title: Attitudes towards Vaccinations in a National Italian Cohort of Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease
pmc-10611209.creator: Andrea Costantino, Marco Michelon, Daniele Noviello, Fabio Salvatore Macaluso, Salvo Leone, Nicole Bonaccorso, Claudio Costantino, Maurizio Vecchi, Flavio Caprioli
pmc-10611209.description: Background: The vaccination status of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) should be investigated before starting any treatment, and patients should eventually be vaccinated against vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs). Patients with IBD may have suboptimal vaccination rates. The aim of this study was to evaluate the vaccination coverage, attitude towards vaccinations, and determinants among an Italian cohort of patients with IBD.

pmc-11319892.title: Cerebral Microbleeds in Different Brain Regions and Their Associations With the Digital Clock-Drawing Test: Secondary Analysis of the Framingham Heart Study
pmc-11319892.creator: Samia C Akhter-Khan, Qiushan Tao, Ting Fang Alvin Ang, Cody Karjadi, Indira Swetha Itchapurapu, David J Libon, Michael Alosco, Jesse Mez, Wei Qiao Qiu, Rhoda Au
pmc-11319892.description: BackgroundCerebral microbleeds (CMB) increase the risk for Alzheimer disease. Current neuroimaging methods that are used to detect CMB are costly and not always accessible.ObjectiveThis study aimed to explore whether the digital clock-drawing test (DCT) may provide a behavioral indicator of CMB.

pmc-11433574.title: Comparison of Dye Spread Pattern and Nerve Involvement between Suprainguinal and Infrainguinal Fascia Iliaca Blocks with Different Injectate Volumes: A Cadaveric Evaluation
pmc-11433574.creator: Tae-Hyeon Cho, Byongnam Jun, Hun-Mu Yang, Shin Hyung Kim
pmc-11433574.description: Background and Objectives: Fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) is an effective and relatively safe technique in perioperative pain management for hip surgery. However, blockade of the obturator nerve (ON) using this technique remains controversial. This study aimed to compare dye spread patterns and nerve involvement in the suprainguinal FICB (S-FICB) and infrainguinal FICB (I-FICB) approaches using different volumes of dye.

pmc-11435846.title: Accuracy Validation of a Sensor-Based Inertial Measurement Unit and Motion Capture System for Assessment of Lower Limb Muscle Strength in Older Adults—A Novel and Convenient Measurement Approach
pmc-11435846.creator: Ye Zhu, Haojie Li, Xie Wu, Nan Chen, Alan Godfrey, Diana Trojaniello
pmc-11435846.description: (1) Background: The aim of this study was to assess lower limb muscle strength in older adults during the transfer from sitting to standing (STS) using an inertial measurement unit (IMU). Muscle weakness in this population can severely impact function and independence in daily living and increase the risk of falls.

pmc-11511775.title: Serum antibodies against mimotopes of Merkel cell polyomavirus oncoproteins detected by a novel immunoassay in healthy individuals and Merkel cell carcinoma patients
pmc-11511775.creator: Chiara Mazziotta, Giada Badiale, Christian Felice Cervellera, Giulia Tonnini, Milena Oimo, Antoine Touzé, Françoise Arnold, Stefania Zanussi, Ornella Schioppa, Giuseppe Fanetti, Mauro Tognon, Fernanda Martini, John Charles Rotondo
pmc-11511775.description: Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) is the foremost causative factor of Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC), a rare yet highly aggressive skin cancer. Although the evaluation of circulating IgG antibodies against Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) LT/sT oncoproteins is clinically useful for MCC diagnosis/prognosis, a limited number of assays for identifying such antibodies have been developed.

pmc-11589873.title: An energy-resolving photon-counting X-ray detector for computed tomography combining silicon-photomultiplier arrays and scintillation crystals
pmc-11589873.creator: Kenji Shimazoe, Donghwan Kim, Moh Hamdan, Yosuke Kobayashi, Kei Kamada, Masao Yoshino, Yasuhiro Shoji, Kyohei Sakamoto, Fabio Acerbi, Alberto Gola
pmc-11589873.description: X-ray photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) has garnered considerable interest owing to its low-dose administration, high-quality imaging, and material decomposition characteristics. Current commercial PCCT systems employ compound semiconductor photon-counting X-ray detectors, which offer good energy resolution. However, the choice of materials is limited, and cadmium telluride or cadmium zinc telluride is mostly used.

pmc-11615895.title: Proteomics and Incident Kidney Failure in Individuals With CKD: The African American Study of Kidney Disease and Hypertension and the Boston Kidney Biopsy Cohort
pmc-11615895.creator: Teresa K Chen, Aditya L Surapaneni, Insa M Schmidt, Sushrut S Waikar, Josef Coresh, Hongbo Liu, Katalin Susztak, Eugene P Rhee, Celina Liu, Pascal Schlosser, Morgan E Grams
pmc-11615895.description: Rationale & ObjectiveIndividuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at increased risk of morbidity and mortality, particularly as they progress to kidney failure. Identifying circulating proteins that underlie kidney failure development may guide the discovery of new targets for intervention.Study DesignProspective cohort.

pmc-12421945.title: Water as a Compass: Hydrostimulation‐Triggered Aerial Root Growth in Phalaenopsis aphrodite
pmc-12421945.creator: Hua‐Chen Chang, I‐Chian Chen, Jhun‐Chen Chen, Yueh‐Ju Hou, Su‐Chiung Fang
pmc-12421945.description: Epiphytic orchids have evolved specialized adaptive strategies, such as aerial roots with water‐absorbing velamen tissues, to cope with water‐scarce and nutrient‐deficient habitats. Our previous study revealed that the aerial roots of the epiphytic orchid Phalaenopsis aphrodite lack a gravitropic response, raising the possibility that alternative tropic mechanisms may contribute to their adaptation.

pmc-12468133.title: Exogenous Sugar Alleviates Salt Stress in Cucumber Seedlings by Regulating the Antioxidant System and Hormone Signaling
pmc-12468133.creator: Guangchao Yu, Zhipeng Wang, Ming Wei, Lian Jia, Yue Qu, Yingyi Jiang, Zhaohui Chu
pmc-12468133.description: This study explored the regulatory effects of exogenous glucose (Glu) and sucrose (Suc) on the growth performance and physiological mechanisms of cucumber seedlings under salt stress. Using two cucumber cultivars as experimental materials, pot experiments demonstrated that salt stress significantly suppressed seedling growth, decreased chlorophyll content, and triggered oxidative damage.

pmc-12554186.title: Colchicine and cardiovascular outcomes in MINOCA: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-12554186.creator: Peter Oro, Aravinthan Vignarajah, Joseph El Dahdah, Nishanthi Vigneswaramoorthy, Yousif Awakeem, Gautam V Shah
pmc-12554186.description: BackgroundMINOCA accounts for 5 %–15 % of myocardial infarctions and is defined by <50 % coronary stenosis without an alternative diagnosis, with heterogeneous mechanisms that complicate care. Given the role of inflammation and microvascular dysfunction, we evaluated whether colchicine improves outcomes.

pmc-12651034.title: Advances in Multi-Omics Research on Biomarkers of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma
pmc-12651034.creator: Jingxue Yang, Jintong Na, Tieliu Shi, Xiyu Liu, Ralf Weiskirchen, Dileep G Nair
pmc-12651034.description: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is a rare yet aggressive malignancy characterized by late-stage diagnosis and poor prognosis. Recent advancements in multi-omics technologies have significantly enhanced the understanding of the molecular features and complex biological mechanisms of iCCA. These approaches have revealed disease molecular heterogeneity and identified biomarkers linked to disease progression, patient prognosis, and therapeutic outcomes.

pmc-13084747.title: Quality as part of universal health coverage in Bhutan: a narrative synthesis
pmc-13084747.creator: Jayendra Sharma, Milena Pavlova, Wim Groot
pmc-13084747.description: SummaryQuality of care is fundamental for countries’ progress towards universal health coverage (UHC). While access to health care and financial protection have received substantial attention in both global- and country-level discussions and monitoring systems, attention to quality of care in the context of UHC has remained rather limited.

pmc-13212755.title: Compassionate Understanding in Dementia Care
pmc-13212755.creator: Steve Matthews
pmc-13212755.description: Practitioners of person-centred care (PCC) for people living with dementia aspire to preserve and honour personhood through respect, relational care, and the promotion of agency and interests; yet its practical realisation often falters. This paper isolates an important moral-psychological element required for PCC’s fulfilment: the professional stance of compassionate understanding.

pmc-13234180.title: A GAN-physical simulation coupled framework for joint optimization of building energy prediction and spatial configuration
pmc-13234180.creator: Liu JinYan
pmc-13234180.description: Building energy optimization faces challenges in simultaneously addressing spatial design and energy performance prediction. This paper proposes a novel framework integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs) with physics-based simulation engines to achieve joint optimization of building energy consumption prediction and spatial configuration.

pmc-13388409.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Model for Predicting Sepsis and Septic Shock Among Patients with Documented Fever at Emergency Department Triage Using Patients’ Historical Data
pmc-13388409.creator: Seung Jin Maeng, Ye Rim Lee, Se Uk Lee, Jae Yong Yu, Jung Won Choi, Guntak Lee, Jong Eun Park, Tae Gun Shin, Sung Yeon Hwang, Hee Yoon, Won Chul Cha, Taerim Kim, Minha Kim, Hansol Chang, Sejin Heo
pmc-13388409.description: This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning-based scoring system for predicting sepsis and septic shock among febrile patients at emergency department (ED) triage using longitudinal data. This retrospective, single-center study included adult patients, presented to ED of tertiary academic hospital with fever from January 2016 to December 2021.
